Carve: Dealing physical damage to champions reduces the target's Armor by 6% for 6 seconds. (stacks 5 times).

Damage modifier (amplification/reduction) — Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.

Penetration and resistance reduction — Effects that reduce the target's effective resistances before mitigation: percent penetration applies before flat penetration, results cannot go below 0, and only resistance reduction effects can drive armor/MR negative.

step_1_magnitudes_are_faithful.claim: Every raw number in the removed object matches the cached wiki text for Carve.
step_1_magnitudes_are_faithful.work: 5 stacks × 6% per stack = 30% = 0.30 armor reduction (S1, S2). Stack duration 6.0 s (S1, S2). expires_at 13.5 − duration 6.0 => applied at t = 7.5 s. Target Aatrox is a champion, so Carve is applicable.
step_1_magnitudes_are_faithful.conclusion: The value is not a fabricated or stale number. 'both_wrong' is ruled out on magnitude grounds.

step_2_category_check.claim: Carve is a resistance-reduction (armor shred) effect, NOT a damage modifier; an entry of kind 'damage_modifier' carrying amount/applied_amount = 0.3 is a category error under the cached wiki taxonomy.
step_2_category_check.work: S3 defines damage.modifier as 'Independent damage value modifiers **distinct from resistances**' — the family Bloodsong's Expose Weakness belongs to (S8: '+8%/5% increased damage from all sources'). S4 places armor shred in damage.penetration / resistance reduction. S5 shows the engine's own composition already carries percentage armor reduction inside the resistance chain R ← R·(1−r_pct/100) before penetration and before mitigation m(R)=100/(100+R). A support-ledger 'damage_modifier' whose amount and applied_amount are the armor fraction (0.3) is therefore either (a) a double count of a reduction already applied in the resistance path, or (b) at best a mislabeled informational row that any consumer summing applied_amount over damage_modifier events reads as a 30% damage amplifier.

numeric_demonstration.point: 30% armor reduction is worth +19.5% damage here, not +30%. Booking 0.30 as a damage_modifier amount overstates Carve by ~10 percentage points of damage on top of a shred the resistance path has already applied.

step_3_stack_state_check.claim: A hard 5.0 stacks / 0.30 entry is also inconsistent with the engine's documented Black Cleaver model.
step_3_stack_state_check.work: S6 pins the modeled reduction to average stacks: constant model 0.8 × 5 = 4.0 stacks => 24% (0.24); exact Cesàro mean of the capped ramp over h hits = 5 − 10/h stacks => h=10: 4.00 (24.0%), h=17: 4.41 (26.5%), h=18: 4.44 (26.7%). No documented model yields a flat 5.0 stacks / 0.30 for the fight.
step_3_stack_state_check.conclusion: Supporting, not decisive: a per-application ledger could legitimately show the ramp topping out at 5 stacks. But it means the removed row is not the number the damage path uses, so its removal cannot be a damage regression.

step_4_window_boundary_check.claim: The removed row's active window [7.5, 13.5] starts at the last authored timestamp in the ledger and runs almost entirely past the fight.
step_4_window_boundary_check.work: The row is the LAST element (index 17) of support_events and the only reported member change, so nothing after it was displaced. If the ledger's Carve applications are one-per-physical-hit on the periodic swing schedule t_i = i·Δ (S7), then index 17 at t = 7.5 s forces Δ = 7.5/17 = 0.4412 s, i.e. AS·u = 2.2667/s and AS·u·T = 17.0 exactly at T = 7.5 s. S7's convention then gives N(T) = ⌊17.0⌋ = 17 legal hits (indices 0–16) and excludes the hit landing exactly at T — which is precisely index 17. The fencepost is self-consistent: the removed row is the classic at-boundary off-by-one.
step_4_window_boundary_check.conclusion: Inferred, not proven (the fight duration is not in data/), but it is the only reading under which every quoted number lines up, and it independently predicts exactly this one row being dropped.

step_5_what_absence_costs.work: Carve refreshes to 5 stacks on every physical hit and each stack lasts 6 s (S1). With hits at ~0.44 s intervals, the 30% shred is already carried by the earlier ledger rows across the whole fight; the dropped row adds a window that begins at the boundary and expires at 13.5 s, after the fight. Removing it therefore removes no in-window shred.
step_5_what_absence_costs.conclusion: Absence contradicts no wiki number. Presence, as a damage_modifier row worth 0.30, does contradict the taxonomy (S3/S4) and the resistance composition (S5).

verdict_reasoning: The old row's magnitudes are exactly right for Carve as an armor reduction (5 × 6% = 30%, 6 s — S1/S2), so the number is not wrong; that rules out 'both_wrong'. But nothing in the cached wiki text or in docs/math-foundations.md supports Carve existing as a 'damage_modifier' support event with amount/applied_amount 0.30: the wiki taxonomy explicitly separates damage modifiers from resistance effects (S3/S4), and math-foundations already applies percentage armor reduction inside the resistance composition (S5), where 30% shred on a level-18 Aatrox is worth +19.5% damage, not +30%. On top of that, the row's hard 5.0 stacks contradicts the documented average-stack model (S6), and its window [7.5, 13.5] is the at-boundary application S7's counting convention excludes. Its disappearance loses no in-window shred. Therefore the new state (absent) is the defensible one.
caveats_and_alternate_hypothesis: This oracle deliberately never read src/, tests/, scripts/, the diff, or the plan, so the membership rule for support_events is inferred from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md only.

Alternate hypothesis considered and rejected: support_events is a purely informational cross-participant ledger in which Carve's team-wide shred (armor reduction is a debuff on the target, so allies benefit) is legitimately listed. Rejected because the row's generic amount/applied_amount fields carry the armor fraction verbatim — the exact shape that lets a consumer read 30% shred as a 30% damage amp — and because the same debuff is already represented by earlier rows and by the resistance path.

If, contrary to step 4, the fight window extends well past 7.5 s and support_events is the enemy's active-debuff view rather than a damage-modifier feed, the correct fix would have been to relabel the row (kind/field naming), not to keep it as-is — so 'old_value_correct' still would not follow.
